Yes—paper [1] gives a probabilistic upper bound on how far the actor parameter stays from the optimum in a slow-fast two-timescale actor-critic setting. It states that, with high probability, after some finite time the actor error stays in a safe region, and gives an explicit bound on \(\|\theta_k-\theta^*\|\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). [1]

Paper [3] is also about two-timescale methods in reinforcement learning, but it focuses on stability and convergence under Markovian noise rather than an explicit high-probability bound for actor error. [3]
